title: Unity game developer (C# / shaders / gameplay)
description: A 5-year Unity gameplay engineer evaluated against 8 postings: a strong game-studio match with netcode gaps, a live-ops mobile Unity role, a marginal AR/VR industrial-visualization role, and five distractors spanning web, backend, DevOps, community, and analytics.
rationale: This scenario stresses cross-domain transfer of a Unity/C# skill set: the same engine skills appear in game studios, industrial AR/VR, and nowhere else, and the matcher must separate those domains from surface-level 'games' vocabulary. j1 and j2 are game-studio roles on the resume's exact stack (grades 3 and 2; j2 is 2 because its live-ops mobile focus differs from the resume's current PC gameplay emphasis, though the resume did ship two mobile F2P titles). j3 is the deliberate marginal case: AR/VR industrial visualization shares Unity, C#, and 3D math but sits in a different domain and demands an XR/CAD stack (OpenXR, MRTK, Pixyz) the resume lacks, hence grade 1. j7 (community manager at a game studio) shares the games domain but not the engineering family, testing that domain words alone do not rank; j4/j5/j6/j8 are web, backend, DevOps, and analytics roles with no core-stack overlap, all grade 0. Gap target j1 overlaps heavily on C#, Unity, HLSL/Shader Graph, Profiler, and Addressables while requiring multiplayer netcode the resume clearly lacks (high) and preferring DOTS/ECS, FMOD, and console certification (low).

resume.summary: Game developer with 5 years of experience building gameplay systems and shaders in Unity. Shipped three titles across PC and mobile, owning features from prototype to live release with a focus on combat systems, designer tooling, and rendering performance.

jobs.raw_text:
Gameplay Engineer — Foxglove Interactive (Hybrid, Austin TX)

Foxglove is a 40-person studio building a 4-player co-op action game in Unity for PC and consoles.

What you will do:
- Own gameplay systems: abilities, enemy AI behaviors, and player progression
- Implement and debug multiplayer gameplay on our Netcode for GameObjects stack
- Write and optimize HLSL and Shader Graph effects alongside our tech artists
- Profile and fix CPU/GPU hotspots with the Unity Profiler and manage content via Addressables

Requirements: C#, Unity, gameplay systems experience, multiplayer netcode (Netcode for GameObjects or Photon), HLSL or Shader Graph. 5+ years of game programming and at least one shipped Unity title. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent shipped-title experience.

Nice to have: Unity DOTS/ECS, FMOD audio middleware, console certification experience.

Senior Unity Developer — Lanternfish Games (Remote, US)

Lanternfish operates two live free-to-play mobile titles with 5M combined MAU. We are hiring a senior Unity developer for our live-ops team.

You will build and ship new gameplay features and seasonal live events, optimize memory and frame rate for low-end Android and iOS devices, extend our Addressables content-delivery pipeline, and harden client stability against crash regressions.

Requirements: C#, Unity, mobile performance optimization, live-ops feature development. 4+ years of professional Unity development with at least one shipped mobile title. Bonus: Firebase Analytics, in-app purchase integration.

AR/VR Visualization Engineer — Corten Industrial (Onsite, Detroit MI)

Corten builds AR/VR training simulations and digital-twin visualizations for automotive manufacturers.

You will build interactive 3D visualizations of production lines in Unity, integrate CAD data through Pixyz import pipelines, develop and deploy for HoloLens and Quest headsets, and gather requirements onsite with enterprise clients.

Requirements: C#, Unity, 3D math, XR SDKs (OpenXR, MRTK), CAD data handling. 3+ years in Unity or real-time 3D visualization. Bonus: manufacturing domain experience, multi-user session synchronization.
